quote: 1. I've also never hung onto a security if the reason I bought it has changed.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 2. What you have to look at is what people think it's going to earn. If you can see something in two years is going to be entirely different than the conventional wisdom, that's how you make money.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 3. My goal is just to become a better and better trader, more and more disciplined, so I can be more and more successful in the market. I am disciplined in implementing the system and sticking to it.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 4. With every trade I make, my approach is always 'risk-first.' By thinking and acting 'risk-first,' you know exactly what you stand to lose if you're wrong, which in trading is far more important than what you stand to gain if you're right.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 5. If you want to make money in the market, if you want to be successful in anything, you really got to put in a lot of time.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 6. My longevity stems from the fact that I try to control risk as much as possible. When the market starts down I sell quickly and don't let the losses get out of hand.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 7. I'm always thinking about losing money as opposed to making money. Don't focus on making money, focus on protecting what you have.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 8. I believe the best way to manage risk is to be bullish when you have a compelling risk/reward and bearish when you don't.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 9. The market is the greatest humbling device in the world.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 10. Unrequited love in the stock market can be very expensive.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 11. A loss never bothers me after I take it. I might be wrong on a stock more than once in a row, but I'm not going to be wrong for very long.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 12. You want to be involved in a stock while it is undergoing accumulation, not distribution.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 13. You should not risk more than you expect to gain on average; I call that the 'Cardinal Sin.'
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 14. If you normally cut losses at 7 to 8 percent, cut them at 5 to 6 percent.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 15. My percentage of winners is only about 50/50, because I cut my losers very quickly.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 16. With each buy order I enter, I know the exact price where I am going to sell at a loss if things don't work out as expected. I define this price level before I get in.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 17. Everyone makes mistakes; that's unavoidable. But not correcting a mistake or minimizing the damage of a position gone wrong is completely under your own control. The big mistakes start out as small mistakes that were allowed to get out of hand. You must realize that big losses are a choice and take responsibility for controlling them.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 18. If it reenters its base, I have a rule to cut at least 50 percent of the position.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 19. I'm only rich because I know when I'm wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 20. Growth comes at the expense of comfort.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 21. There is a lot more noise and movement in the market with high speed trading and computerized algorithms, but the stocks that have the biggest moves continue to have the same characteristics.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 22. I've never made a buy at a low that I didn't just feel terrible and scared to death making it. It's easy to sell at the bottom. You can go home that night and it relieves you of your nerves.

quote: 23. It's better to lose correctly than to win incorrectly.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 24. I usually hold my big winners for about six to twelve months, stocks that aren't that strong about three months, and my losers less than two weeks.

quote: 25. Hope is not a strategy.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 26. Those who succeed big at anything all have the same attitude: You keep going until it happens or you die trying. Quitting is not an option.

quote: 30. Figuring yourself out and developing a discipline are probably the most important things.

quote: 33. What I learned from George Soros was sizing is 70 or 80 percent of the equation.

quote: 35. If you want to mitigate risk effectively, you simply must acknowledge that stocks don't manage themselves. You're the manager, and it's up to you to protect your hard-earned capital.

speaker: David Ryan

quote: 37. If you look at what the Fed did, the radical gamble they took to get inflation up 30 basis points from 1.7 to 2, it's, to me, sort of a risk-reward bet. You bet 1 to lose 40? And they lost.

quote: 38. This is the biggest redistribution of wealth from the middle class and the poor to the rich ever.

quote: 39. The key is to see things as they are—operating in the now—without seeing things as worse than they are out of fear, or better than they are out of greed.

quote: 45. Soros has taught me that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular. It takes courage to be a pig.

quote: 46. Bad news is sometimes the best buying opportunity life gives you.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 47. Amateurs think about how much money they can make. Professionals think about how much money they could lose.

quote: 48. Trade what you see, not what you think.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 49. If you're extremely confident, taking a loss doesn't bother you.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 50. When I've looked at all the investors that have very large reputations — Warren Buffett, Carl Icahn, George Soros — they all only have one thing in common. It is to make large concentrated bets where they have a lot of conviction.

quote: 51. Stocks should be at a profit the first day you buy them.

quote: 52. Not losing big is the single most important factor for winning big. As a speculator, losing is not a choice, but how much you lose is.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 53. Soros is the best loss taker I've ever seen. He doesn't care whether he wins or loses on a trade. If a trade doesn't work, he's confident enough about his ability to win on other trades that he can easily walk away from the position.

quote: 54. Looking at the biggest winners, we found that in many cases, the earnings had been on the table for a while.

quote: 55. The first thing I heard when I got in the business - not from my mentor - was, 'Bulls make money, bears make money, and pigs get slaughtered.' I'm here to tell you I was a pig.

quote: 56. You must adjust your risk as a function of potential reward.

quote: 57. I try not to get too complicated. I look at the daily Dow and that works but it's not foolproof.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 58. Look at your own life. You can get so many stock ideas from just what you're buying. … From examining your own life, you can come up with unbelievable, great investing ideas.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 59. The way to build superior long-term returns is through preservation of capital and home runs.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 60. There's no reason you should always be long. If you're sure a bear market is coming — go to cash.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 61. Success in investing doesn't correlate with I.Q. once you're above the level of 125. Once you have ordinary intelligence, what you need is the temperament to control the urges that get other people into trouble in investing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 62. In investing, when I hear the word 'conviction' I run like a deer. All the biggest financial collapses in history were caused by smart people with conviction. I would bet on a person with average intelligence that respects risk over a genius with conviction any day of the week.

quote: 63. The cup-and-handle is one of the better ones but it does not show up nearly as often as people might think. A cup-and-handle really has to occur in a general market correction.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 64. My favorite quote of all time is maybe Mark Twain: 'Put all your eggs in one basket and watch the basket carefully.' I tend to think that's what great investors do.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 65. To have lasting success in the stock market, you must decide once and for all that it's more important to make money than to be right. Your ego must take a backseat.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 66. Learn to buy weakness and sell strength, and not buy strength and sell weakness; because you're just going to continue to get whipsawed.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 67. Calculating risks shrewdly is the main ingredient for consistent superior performance. Pros play percentage ball, and that's why, in the long run, they are more consistent than amateurs.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 68. Too many investors look at the present. The present is already in the price. You have to think out of the box and visualize 18-24 months from now, what the world is going to be and what securities might trade at.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 69. I look for support points that have held in the past or previous highs the stock has pulled back down on to.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 70. The wonderful thing about our business is that it's liquid, and you can wipe the slate clean on any day.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 71. The single most important advice I can give anybody is: Learn from your mistakes. That is the only way to become a successful trader.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 72. Virtually every superperformance phase in big, winning stocks occurred while the stock price was in a definite price uptrend. In almost every case, the trend was identifiable early in the superperformance advance.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 73. I think diversification and all the stuff they're teaching at business school today is probably the most misguided concept everywhere.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 74. If you're early on in your career and they give you a choice between a great mentor or higher pay, take the mentor every time. It's not even close.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 75. Your stop loss should be a calculation as a function of expected gain. Then you back into risk based on your own personal math. That's the holy grail; managing the risk/reward relationship.

quote: 76. Trading without a stop-loss is like driving a car without brakes. Those who trade without stops, eventually stop trading.

quote: 77. I think investment psychology is by far the most important element, followed by risk control, with the least important consideration being the question of where you buy and sell.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 78. One of my favorite patterns is the tendency for the markets to move from relative lows to relative highs and vice versa every two to four days... It takes several days of a market rallying before it looks really good. That's when everyone wants to buy it, and that's the time when the professionals, like myself, are selling. Conversely, when the market has been down for a few days, and everyone is bearish, that's the time I like to be buying.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 79. To compound your money, and not your mistakes, your goal is to buy on the way up—not on the way down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 80. If you don't feel like a fool, you're not managing risk.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 81. You must have a love for the market in order to be successful in this game.

quote: 82. Do not invest in the present. The present is not what moves stock prices.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 83. Long-term success in the stock market has nothing to do with hope or luck. Winning stock traders have rules and a well-thought-out plan. Conversely, losers lack rules, or if they have rules, they don't stick to them for very long; they deviate.

quote: 84. I cut the losers very quickly. The maximum loss I allow is 7%.

speaker: Mark Minervini

speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 89. Chart patterns are not the cause; they're the effect. Human behavior hasn't changed and isn't likely to change much in the future.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 90. You can tell a lot by volume. If the volume doubles one day and the stock moves to a new high, it is telling you a lot of people are interested in the stock and buying it.
speaker: David Ryan
